The '''Chinka-sai''' (鎮火祭), also known as the "Fire Extinguishing Festival," is a traditional Japanese ritual dedicated to fire prevention and expressing gratitude for the blessings of fire. Originating in the Nara period (710–794 AD), it was historically referred to as "Hoshizume-no-matsuri" or "Hishizume-no-matsuri." Traditionally, on the night of the last day of the 6th and 12th lunar months, rituals were conducted at the four corners of the imperial palace by the {{ill|Urabe clan|ja|卜部氏|en|draft:Yoshida family|lt=Urabe clan}}, who were diviners. These ceremonies aimed to pacify the fire deity and prevent calamities associated with fire. <ref>https://kotobank.jp/word/%E9%8E%AE%E7%81%AB%E7%A5%AD-98603</ref>.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2024-05-06|title=Chinka-sai (hana shizume matsuri) {{!}} 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240506033126/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9293|access-date=2024-05-06|website=web.archive.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2024-05-06|title=Chinka-sai (hi/ho shizume no matsuri) {{!}} 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240506033305/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9292|access-date=2024-05-06|website=web.archive.org}}</ref>
{{User:Immanuelle/Ritual ceremonies of the Imperial Palace updated}}
In contemporary times, various Shinto shrines across Japan continue to observe the Chinka-sai. Notable examples include:
* '''Itsukushima Shrine''' in Hiroshima Prefecture: Held annually on December 31st, this festival, also known as the "Fire Prevention Festival," is conducted on the shores of Mikasa-hama. The ritual involves lighting a sacred fire (imibi) in the shrine's purification hall, transferring it to torches, and then igniting a large torch on the beach. Participants create torches of varying sizes, and after receiving the sacred fire, they extinguish them and take them home as protective charms against fire hazards for the coming year. * '''Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen Shrine''' in Yamanashi Prefecture: Known as the "[[Yoshida Fire Festival|Yoshida Fire Festival]]" or "Chinka-sai," this event is held annually on August 26th and 27th. The festival is renowned for the lighting of large torches throughout the town, symbolizing the pacification of Mount Fuji's volcanic eruptions and marking the end of the climbing season. The sight of numerous torches illuminating the night is considered one of Japan's most unique and spectacular festivals.   Sengen Shrine
The Chinka-sai serves as a significant cultural event, fostering community bonds and preserving traditional practices centered around fire, a vital element in daily life and spirituality in Japan.
